newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says wages to moderate as growth slows.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says wages to moderate as growth slows.

text.p: Wage increases in Singapore should moderate in 1997 in line with the economy's slower pace of growth since last year, the Ministry of Labour said in a statement on Saturday.

The ministry said it agreed with a National Wages Council (NWC) recommendation that the total wage increase for 1997 should be moderated as the economy was projected to grow between five and seven percent, compared with seven percent growth last year and 8.8 percent in 1995.
The NWC said on Friday it expected a 1997 average wage increase of less than last year's 6.7 percent.
Built-in wage increases should lag productivity growth and additional rewards should be given in the form of a variable component based on a company's performance, the labour ministry said.
Singapore's labour market remained tight with 102,600 jobs created last year, it said.
Although the number of redundancies rose to 11,000 from 8,800 in 1995, the ministry said retrenched workers generally had no difficulty finding alternative employment.
"Retrenchments are not unexpected as our economy restructures towards higher value-added activities, and in view of the slowdown in our economy," the statement said.
